cldap_rootdse_disclosure.title: CLDAP rootDSE Information Disclosure
cldap_rootdse_disclosure.description: The host responds to Connectionless LDAP (CLDAP) rootDSE queries on UDP/389. The rootDSE entry discloses domain naming context, DNS hostname, server name, and other directory metadata to anyone reaching the port.
cldap_rootdse_disclosure.impact: Reveals the AD domain DN (e.g., `DC=corp,DC=example,DC=local`) and DC hostname. Attackers use this for AD reconnaissance — feeding the info into BloodHound, ldapsearch, or kerbrute follow-ups.
cldap_rootdse_disclosure.remediation: CLDAP is typically only used by AD clients during discovery. If this host is internal-only, restrict UDP/389 at the firewall. If external CLDAP access is required (rare), disable rootDSE response via the AD LDAP policy (requires careful testing — some AD client workflows depend on it).
cldap_rootdse_disclosure.evidence_template: CLDAP rootDSE query against {{host}}:389 returned defaultNamingContext: {{default_naming_context}}

cldap_service_responding.title: CLDAP Service Responding on UDP/389
cldap_service_responding.description: A Connectionless LDAP (CLDAP) service on UDP/389 answered an unauthenticated rootDSE query. No directory attributes were returned.
cldap_service_responding.impact: Confirms a CLDAP responder is reachable, which narrows an attacker's target list and exposes the host to CLDAP reflection/amplification abuse. No directory information was disclosed by this query, so this is an attack-surface observation rather than an information disclosure.
cldap_service_responding.remediation: CLDAP is normally only needed by Active Directory clients during domain discovery. If this host is not a domain controller serving external clients, restrict UDP/389 at the network boundary. If the responder is unexpected on this host, identify the listening service — CLDAP responders on non-AD devices are frequently a misconfiguration.
cldap_service_responding.evidence_template: CLDAP rootDSE query against {{host}}:389 received a response containing no directory attributes.
